newsitem.title: HUNGARY: La Lyonnaise, RWE get stake in Budapest waterworks.
newsitem.headline: La Lyonnaise, RWE get stake in Budapest waterworks.

text.p: A consortium made up of 51 percent of La Lyonnaise des Eaux and 49 percent of RWE Aqua, part of the German group RWE, signed on Tuesday a 25-year water management and distribution contract with Budapest, officials said.
"We are here for the long term and not to make a quick mark or franc," RWE Director Richard Klein told a news conference after the signing.
Under the deal, the consortium bought 25 percent plus one share of the Budapest water company, Fovarosi Vizmuvek, which provides the city's water and employs 2,200.
The investment is worth a total $91.6 million, city hall officials said.
The consortium will have management rights, but all investment decisions will have to be taken in accordance with the Budapest council, Mayor Gabor Demszky said.
Another official said the consortium will receive part of the operating cost savings but will not be entitled to a dividend.

RWE already has stakes in the Budapest Electricity Works (ELMU), regional electricity distribution company EDASZ and the Matrai power station and also plans to build a three-billion-mark coal-fired plant in north-east Hungary.
RWE also operates a waste disposal unit in the city of Miskolc.
Lyonnaise des Eaux already manages the waterworks of the south Hungarian cities of Kaposvar and Pecs.
